statement: For every five distinct odd primes 3 <= p_1 < p_2 < p_3 < p_4 < p_5 and every five positive integers a_1,...,a_5, let n=product_{i=1}^5 p_i^{a_i} and R=product_{i=1}^5 p_i. If sigma(n)>=2n and sigma(d)<2d for every positive proper divisor d of n, then there exists i in {1,2,3,4,5} such that p_i^{a_i+1}<2R. This includes sigma(n)=2n and has no bound on primes or exponents. The claim is exactly the frozen original five-prime assertion; no assertion for six or more primes or for the stronger R bound is submitted.
contribution: A complete proof of the odd five-prime case of the small-component 2R conjecture, extending the nearest inspected primary result for three and four odd prime factors. The exponent-uniform quotient estimate forces R-2phi(R) to be 1 or 3 under a counterexample; a congruence excludes 1, and a complete 13-prefix factor certificate excludes 3. All 95 divisor checks leave six ordered integral pairs, each with an explicit composite member; direct last-prime enumeration over 937 possible fourth values agrees. The proof avoids a classification of primitive non-deficient numbers. No covering result was verified in the bounded primary-literature screen of 2026-09-12; global priority and novelty of the elementary inequalities or factorization are not asserted. This is a proposer candidate awaiting fresh referee review.
